episode_title: What a US Investment Bank MD Really Looks for When Hiring Graduates

real_qa.q: What career path did Jamie Phillip take before becoming J.P. Morgan Managing Director?
real_qa.r: Jamie Phillip started his career in operations at an investment bank straight from university, then moved to his first front-office role as a junior dealer at Aspic Capital, a systematic hedge fund. After several years on the buy side executing trades, he moved to the sell side at age 26-27 to start up a commodity institutional futures desk at a smaller bank with one other person, building up a book of business before eventually moving to J.P. Morgan where he spent nearly 19 years.
real_qa.requete: Jamie Phillip career path J.P. Morgan

real_qa.q: What key attributes does a J.P. Morgan Managing Director look for when hiring graduate candidates?
real_qa.r: Jamie Phillip focuses on fit within the team, hunger to succeed, and whether candidates are teachable. He emphasizes avoiding overconfidence, seeking genuine humility, and assessing whether someone wants to make an impact on the business rather than just climb the ladder. He looks for candidates who show consistency, treat everyone the same regardless of seniority, and are open to learning quickly—alarm bells ring when graduates show overconfidence without understanding the real risks of trading floors.
real_qa.requete: J.P. Morgan MD hiring graduates what look for

real_qa.q: Why is consistency critical for success in early-career finance roles?
real_qa.r: Consistency is hugely important because clients and colleagues need to know exactly what they're getting from you every day. Some days are better than others, but there must be clarity and honesty about your performance level. Consistency also builds trust over time with both external clients and internal colleagues—you cannot have a long-term career at a top organization without it, and it comes from having openness in your communications with everybody.

real_qa.q: How should graduates respond to market crises or trading errors in a sales and trading environment?
real_qa.r: The correct response is to immediately raise your hand and flag the problem to your manager or team rather than trying to trade out of it alone. You bring somebody else from your team into the conversation and fix the problem together. This is critical because showing weakness by fessing up to mistakes is actually a strength—in fast-moving markets like the nickel crisis, waiting or trying to handle it yourself is dangerous.
real_qa.requete: trading error crisis how respond immediately flag

real_qa.q: What was Jamie Phillip's experience setting up the J.P. Morgan China joint venture for futures trading?
real_qa.r: In his late 20s and early 30s, Jamie was asked to help set up the China-J.P. Morgan joint venture to trade futures on Chinese exchanges. J.P. Morgan was one of the first international banks to move into this space. The operation was based in Zhongshan on the south coast with five million residents, none of whom worked in finance for a major bank. It required him to relearn how to operate in a completely different culture and market, managing a local team, and was personally and culturally difficult but provided enormous learning.
real_qa.requete: J.P. Morgan China joint venture futures trading

real_qa.q: What separates graduates who thrive from those who struggle in their first years at an investment bank?
real_qa.r: Beyond technical skills, the key is integrating yourself into the business by listening, applying your academic knowledge to the workplace, improving weaknesses, and bringing consistency and honesty to your work every day. Graduates who thrive show a lack of entitlement, willingness to do things differently to make it work for the business, and the ability to be an open book about their values and what they bring to the table—treating everyone the same regardless of their position.
